title: Coefficient of kinetic friction
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the coefficient of kinetic friction, μ = tan(30°) ≈ 0.577 or √3/3, from the condition of constant speed sliding down.

title: Acceleration up the incline
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the acceleration a = 5 m/s² for the block moving up, using Newton's second law with the applied force, gravity, and friction.

title: Time of force application
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the time t = 2 s for which the force is applied, ensuring the block just reaches the top.

title: Force balance for constant speed
description: Important: The solution must establish the force equilibrium (mg sinθ = μ mg cosθ) for the block sliding down at constant speed to find μ.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply Newton's second law separately for the upward acceleration phase and the subsequent deceleration phase after F is removed.

title: Kinematics linking phases
description: Important: The solution must correctly use kinematics (v = at, v² = 2a'x₂) to relate the velocity, time, and displacements of the two motion phases.

title: Total distance constraint
description: Important: The solution must enforce the geometric constraint that the sum of the displacements in the two phases equals the incline length (x₁ + x₂ = l).

title: Sign/direction error in forces
description: Pitfall: Penalize if friction or gravitational force components have incorrect signs/directions in the equations of motion for the upward or deceleration phases.

title: Incorrect deceleration magnitude
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the deceleration a' after force removal is not correctly calculated as g sinθ + μ g cosθ = 10 m/s².
